subject: Proposed MAP & evaluation timeline for Helium AI — pricing/true-up clarifications
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@heliumai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed MAP & evaluation timeline for Helium AI — pricing/true-up clarifications

Hi Sanjay,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a concise MAP draft and a term sheet (term_sheet_draft.pdf) to help align the evaluation milestones with commercial economics. High level: 

- Eval kickoff: week of Oct 4 — 4-week technical pilot (success criteria listed in the doc).
- Commit ramp: if pilot succeeds, commit to 3mo followed by staged commits (10% -> 40% -> 100% by month 6).
- Pricing: initial commit price with step-down discounts tied to committed QPS/throughput milestones.
- True-up window: standard is 90 days after quarter; we flagged this in the term sheet.

Two open items we want to align on before we send to your legal team: 1) definition of billable usage (tokens vs. inference units vs. host-hours), and 2) true-up cadence and price protection period. Those items materially affect economics during ramp.

Can you confirm who from your procurement/legal will own redlines? If you prefer, we can propose specific language for a 60-day compromise on true-ups and a 12-month price-protection period.

Next steps: if this looks okay I’ll loop in our pricing lead (Rishi) and send a redline-ready version for your counsel.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachments: term_sheet_draft.pdf

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@heliumai.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@heliumai.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP & evaluation timeline for Helium AI — pricing/true-up clarifications

Vanessa —

Appreciate the clear MAP. A few quick clarifications from our side before we ring legal: 

1) Billable units: we prefer "inference units" (per-request token calculation + model weight multiplier) because it maps to our billing model. Can Redwood provide an excerpt showing how you calculate that so engineering can validate?
2) True-up: 90 days is long for us. Our treasury team expects a 30-day true-up window or a monthly reconciliation to avoid cash-flow surprise.
3) Price protection: we like a 12-month protection but want an explicit fallback if market GPU spot rates spike.

Procurement will likely redline the term sheet on the true-up and definition language. For now, please have your pricing/legal propose exact clause language we can circulate. Also — can you confirm whether discounts in the term sheet apply to committed usage only or to committed + overage? That will change our forecast.

I'll try to get counsel in the loop this week.

— Sanjay
CTO, Helium AI
sanjay@heliumai.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-23T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP & evaluation timeline for Helium AI — pricing/true-up clarifications

Vanessa / Lauren —

Quick internal read and recommended posture before we send legal-ready language: 

- Usage definition: offer a primary definition as "billable inference units" with a short appendix showing token->IU conversion and model multipliers. That gives Helium the visibility they asked for while keeping our billing consistent.
- True-up window: counter at 60 days (compromise between their 30 and our 90). We can include a monthly interim statement obligation for transparency with final settlement at 60 days.
- Price protection: provide 12-month floor protection for committed pricing, with an explicit carve-in for material increases tied to cloud compute index (we can reference a published index).
- Discounts applicability: recommend discounts apply to committed usage and structured overage tiers (e.g., overage billed at base price, not discounted tier), but offer a blended threshold where if overage exceeds X% for two consecutive quarters, an automatic review triggers retro pricing adjustments — keeps both sides honest.

I've attached a short redline_snippet.docx with suggested phrasing we can drop into the term sheet. If you want, I can draft the final clause language and send to Sanjay directly (to speed up).

Rishi
Head of Pricing & Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline_snippet.docx

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@heliumai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@heliumai.com>
Date: 2026-09-25T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP & evaluation timeline for Helium AI — pricing/true-up clarifications

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks for the quick feedback. I took Rishi's suggestions and we put together a concise compromise in the attached revised_term_sheet.pdf. Key points in plain language: 

- Billable usage: defined as "billable inference units (BIUs)" with an appendix that converts tokens->BIUs by model class. We included the conversion table for your engineers to validate.
- True-up: we propose a 60-day final settlement window plus monthly interim statements (transparent visibility; final adjustments at 60 days).
- Price protection: 12 months on committed pricing; carve-out if cloud compute index increases by >25% in a quarter — triggers review (not automatic repricing).
- Discounts: apply to committed usage; overage billed at base rate. If overage > 30% for two consecutive quarters we trigger a retrospective review and a potential blended credit.

If that sounds reasonable, Rishi can paste the exact clause text into the term sheet and we can circulate to your counsel. For efficiency, we also prepared a DocuSign envelope (https://docusign.com/envelopes/ABC-789) with a non-binding commercial term annex (no signature required yet) so your procurement team can see redline-ready language.

Proposed MAP timeline (recap):
- Oct 4: Pilot kickoff
- Oct 30: Pilot completion + success review
- Nov 1: If successful, 3-month pilot-to-commit conversion starts
- Jan 1: Target full ramp to committed throughput (per MAP schedule)

Let me know if procurement wants different cadence for PO/POI. We aim to keep this on a 30–45 day close once legal agrees the language.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: revised_term_sheet.pdf

Thanks — that readout is helpful and the conversion appendix clarified the BIU math for my engineers. Procurement reviewed the revised_term_sheet.pdf and the proposed compromises look acceptable in principle. A couple of operational asks before we proceed to DocuSign:

- We will prepare a PO referencing RDW-3251 once legal confirms the final redline. Can you confirm an expected date for the redline-ready contract? Our target is sign + PO by Oct 20 to keep the MAP timeline intact.

If you can send the one-pager and the redline by next Tue I’ll push this through procurement. We’ll plan to sign the DocuSign envelope once the legal items are locked.
